feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows broad ownership across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Impact is good, but it would be stronger with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong specialization in enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility through progression at NACo, scope indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and concrete platform/tool references.  
- Writing is generally polished, concise, and professional, with effective use of action-led bullets and relevant recent projects.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, reduced publishing time, campaign performance, search improvement, or video/email results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and more space for achievements.  
- Fix minor style/grammar inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain consistent comma style in lists (“planning, scripting and production” vs. “planning, scripting, and production”); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground scale/recent relevance: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years modernizing public-sector web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct action verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling.”
- Consider adding one concrete differentiator from recent roles, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “50+ publishers,” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Streamline the second sentence to reduce list-like phrasing: “Leads enterprise web modernization, editorial systems, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search for mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies/footer; “AI-enabled search” is more specific and consistent with recent work.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinctive and executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and optimization.”
- Replace broader or repetitive items with sharper, leadership-oriented terms: “Cross-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communications operations.”
- Group related ideas to reduce sprawl and improve scanability; suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Keep “public-sector” hyphenation consistent across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat language already used in the header.
- Several items substantially overlap with Topline Skills; consider making this section more strategic and less tool/function-specific.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make the footer feel more distinctive and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize outcomes, scale, or audience where possible: e.g., “improve policy-content discovery,” “support ongoing campaign expansion,” “extend conference engagement.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use consistent verb tense, include the multiplication sign as “10 × 20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother phrasing.
- Make project names slightly more descriptive if external readers may not know internal campaign titles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with NACo bullets in recent roles; reframe these as selected examples with outcomes rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all items; vary verbs for stronger rhythm.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, technical contribution, and 2–3 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, campaign architecture, and AI-enabled content discovery as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; e.g., combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, time saved, stakeholder teams served, or performance improvements.
- Use stronger consultant verbs: “advised,” “architected,” “implemented,” “optimized,” “launched,” “streamlined,” rather than “consult” or “develop.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal microsites, modular content, toolkits, and AI-enabled search” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level unless you add results.
- “Governance, analytics, workflows, and enterprise web improvement” also echoes the 2022–2024 director role; emphasize post-tenure consulting scope and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, reduce channel-listing, and avoid overlap with the adjacent NACo roles and projects section.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one sharper achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel/video/analytics bullets outcome-led: add metrics such as email growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, turnaround time, or reporting adoption if available.
- Tighten the final bullet to operational impact: “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may duplicate Recent Projects and earlier video bullets; stress strategic buildout and organizational capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level: operational scale, recurring programs, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and publishing consistency.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve efficiency and content quality.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video” and “weekly updates” overlap with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting all video work.
- “Publishing workflows” and “coordination” overlap with the 2022–2024 role; avoid broad governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current differentiators from recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Web governance and publishing standards” if you want closer alignment with recent NACo leadership work.
- Keep wording parallel: use noun phrases only, avoid mixing “leadership,” “planning,” and “messaging” styles.
- If space allows, prioritize skills tied to recent impact: governance, enterprise web strategy, AI-enabled content/search, analytics-informed planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo role bullets on web, email, social, and video leadership.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize platform leadership and execution strengths, not repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a list of tools to a tighter capability statement, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older platform names unless they are current selling points; Drupal should lead given the recent 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Cut “jQuery” unless specifically required for target roles; it dates the profile and adds little at topline level.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “Platform delivery for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages are already repeated in Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tighten it to emphasize decision support, measurement design, and optimization impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & optimization” or “Measurement, reporting & performance insights.”
- Use grouped wording: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets for each tool.
- Replace generic terms with stronger business language: “KPI framework design,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “web performance and search optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and web performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave the full tool inventory below.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize delivery scope and higher-value production leadership rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level skills to outcome-oriented production leadership.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery
- In-house studio and PTZ camera operations
- Multimedia workflows for advocacy, campaigns and recurring programming
- If space allows, replace “video production and editing” with “broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better reflect seniority.
- Keep terms broad; specific tools already appear under “Technical + IT.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Avoid adding software names here; Premiere Pro and related tools are already covered in “Multimedia & Creative Tools.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same message.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize level of use and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, group by strength: “Primary: Drupal | Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider replacing the title with “CMS & Web Platforms” for slightly clearer phrasing.
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add one high-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration)” rather than listing all tools equally.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is near-duplicate of Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; keep one more strategic and this one more tool-focused.
- GitHub Pages may undersell seniority unless it supports a specific project or portfolio need.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery
- Add a second line for delivery/integration tools: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Consider tightening labels to show application, e.g., “serverless scripting” instead of just “Cloudflare Workers” and “deployment automation” instead of just “GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add one concrete qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, such as “Drupal front-end implementation” or “analytics/event tagging implementation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; either remove them there or make this section more tool-specific.
- GTM may also overlap with analytics infrastructure unless positioned here as implementation/tag deployment.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and keep only strongest, most relevant tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Drop lower-value/general tools unless heavily used in recent roles: Basecamp, Trello.
- If true, add a light qualifier to show applied depth: “used to build editorial workflows, approvals, intake systems, and cross-team coordination.”
- Consider retitling to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with your recent leadership work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same idea verbatim elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; listing both can dilute stronger automation/platform signals unless space is ample.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but as written it’s just a vendor list and misses the level of ownership or implementation implied elsewhere in the CV. It would be stronger if framed as platforms used to run enterprise/member communications.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parenthetical form: **(newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment)** to show practical use rather than passive familiarity.
- Keep this item platform-focused; let the work experience carry outcomes like audience size and newsletter cadence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered well in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 roles.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language in Core Competencies, so keep this item specifically about email/member platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely repeats the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the Director role. Make it more specific to methods/capabilities, not just another tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led: “GA4 & event measurement • Behavioral analytics (Microsoft Clarity) • BI reporting (Looker Studio, Power BI) • Data analysis (BigQuery) • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing”
- Replace “Dashboarding” with a stronger outcome-oriented term like “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent impact: “analytics stack modernization” or “measurement strategy” to reflect the NACo work more clearly.
- Keep the list tight; avoid listing tools already emphasized elsewhere unless they add distinct value here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates Topline Skills [3]; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes/capabilities-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the 2022–2024 role, so this section should avoid sounding repetitive.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if possible: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, email volume, or growth in production capacity.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a fuller version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, while guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on setup/build phase rather than scaled operations.
- Avoid repeating website leadership claims already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support plus the standout launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the differentiator: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced member engagement.
- Remove generic phrasing like “contributed to” and “organizational programs”; use direct verbs and NACo-specific context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Multimedia production appears repeatedly in later NACo roles; avoid overemphasizing general content production here.
- “First podcast” is the clearest unique accomplishment—make it the anchor of this item.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities in experience or topline skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative Software**
